cohort: The study included 216 women aged 18-45 with a history of primary cesarean delivery within the last two years, recruited from Fazaia Ruth Pfau Hospitals, Karachi, Pakistan.
finding: The study identified a 49.1% post-cesarean contraceptive uptake, which, along with adherence, was significantly influenced by socio-demographic factors, partner opposition, presence of a handicapped child, and counseling experiences, with IUCDs being the most preferred method.
